'''Eric Felece Curry''' (born February 3, 1970) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] for seven seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) during the 1990s.  He played [[college football]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama Crimson Tide]], and earned consensus [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors.  A first-round pick in the [[1993 NFL draft]], he played professionally for the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], [[Green Bay Packers]] and [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] of the NFL.

==Early life==
Curry was born in [[Thomasville, Georgia]].<ref name=nflprofile>National Football League, Historical Players, [http://www.nfl.com/player/ericcurry/2500260/profile  Eric Curry] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190420104611/http://www.nfl.com/player/ericcurry/2500260/profile |date=April 20, 2019 }}.  Retrieved February 16, 2012.</ref>  He graduated from [[Thomasville High School]],<ref name=dbfprofile>databaseFootball.com, Players, {{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20120324222639/http://www.databasefootball.com/players/playerpage.htm?ilkid=CURRYERI01  Eric Curry]}}.  Retrieved February 16, 2012.</ref> and played for the Thomasville High School Bulldogs [[high school football]] team.

==College career==
Curry accepted an [[athletic scholarship]] to attend the University of Alabama, where he played for coach [[Bill Curry]] and coach [[Gene Stallings]]' [[Alabama Crimson Tide football]] teams from 1989 to 1992.  As a senior in 1992, Curry was recognized as a consensus first-team All-American and the United Press International Lineman of the Year.  He was a member of the Crimson Tide squad that won the first [[SEC Championship Game]] in 1992, and a consensus national championship by defeating the [[1992 Miami Hurricanes football team|Miami Hurricanes]] 34–13 in the [[1993 Sugar Bowl|Sugar Bowl]].  Curry and fellow defensive end [[John Copeland]] were known as the "bookends" during their time at Alabama, and were key players in the Crimson Tide's No. 1 rated defense in 1992.

==Professional career==
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers selected Curry in the first round, with the sixth overall pick, of the 1993 NFL Draft.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1993 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1993/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-31 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en |archive-date=October 30, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181030130727/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1993/draft.htm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>Pro Football Hall of Fame, Draft History, [http://www.profootballhof.com/history/story.aspx?story_id=2029  1993 National Football League Draft] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924122520/http://www.profootballhof.com/history/story.aspx?story_id=2029 |date=September 24, 2015 }}.  Retrieved February 16, 2012.</ref>  He gained notoriety for happily hugging the NFL Commissioner, [[Paul Tagliabue]], after he was picked by the Buccaneers in the draft.  He played for the Buccaneers from {{NFL Year|1993}} to {{NFL Year|1997}}.  He signed a free agent deal with the Green Bay Packers in {{NFL Year|1998}}, but was released during the preseason.<ref>Packers.com, PACKERS SIGN BUCS DE CURRY AS UNRESTRICTED FREE AGENT, [http://nfl.packers.com/news/releases/1998/04/04-01.html] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305070848/http://nfl.packers.com/news/releases/1998/04/04-01.html|date=March 5, 2016}}.  Retrieved October 10, 2012.</ref>   Curry played for the Jacksonville Jaguars from {{NFL Year|1998}} to {{NFL Year|1999}}.<ref name="pfrprofile">{{Cite web |title=Eric Curry Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CurrEr20.htm |access-date=2024-05-23 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>  In seven NFL seasons, Curry played in 75 regular season games, started 44 of them, and contributed 95 tackles, 12.5 quarterback sacks, and seven forced fumbles.<ref name=pfrprofile/>
